text: Single crystals of NiI2 were grown by the chemical vapor transport technique. The starting materials were mixed in a stoichiometric ratio (Ni: I2 = 1: 1, 500 mg in total) and sealed in 7-inch long silica tubes under vacuum. The tubes were placed in a single-zone tube furnace, with one end at the center. The temperature of the furnace was set to 580 °C at 3 °C/minute, dwelt for 60 h, and then set to room temperature at the same rate. Black single crystals formed at the cold end of the tubes as hexagonal thin flakes.

source.title: Field-resilient supercurrent diode in a multiferroic Josephson junction
